title: The reckoning is close, and people are looking elsewhere.
subtitle: Nearness of the account versus a busy, turned-away mind

row.title: not preparing
sub: knowing, but not working for it

then: Late in the Makkan years, the chiefs of Quraysh were busy opposing the Prophet ﷺ. The surah opens with a warning: {idea}the Hour is near{/idea}, yet people are {trap}not working for it or preparing for it{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ explained the heedlessness as being taken up by this world.
now: You know you will stand before Allah one day. You also know the next phone notification, the deadline on Friday, the sale that ends tonight. One of these gets your planning. {trap}The other gets a vague someday.{/trap} {idea}Close does not wait for someday.{/idea}
old: I believe in the Day, so I am not one of the heedless.
new: Heedless is not denying the Day. It is living as if it were far.
try: Tonight, spend two quiet minutes asking: if my account were tomorrow, what would I finish first?

title: Fresh words from their Lord, heard while playing.
subtitle: Listening without letting anything land
then: Revelation was still coming down, new and direct from Allah. Ibn 'Abbas said the Quran was {reward}the most recently revealed Book, pure and unaltered{/reward}. Yet the Quraysh would {trap}listen to it while they played{/trap}.
now: Quran plays in the car while you scroll at the red light. A talk runs in one earbud while you reply to the family group chat. {trap}The words pass through.{/trap} {idea}Nothing stays long enough to move you.{/idea}
old: If I have it playing, I am benefiting from it.
new: A reminder only works when I stop playing long enough to hear it.
try: Listen to one short surah today with nothing else in your hands.

title: Distracted hearts, whispered excuses: he is just a man.
subtitle: The private reasons people give for ignoring truth
then: In private, the leaders of Quraysh agreed on a line: {trap}is this more than a human being like you?{/trap} They could not accept that one of them had been chosen for revelation. They called it magic and warned each other not to submit to it. The verse names the root first: {idea}their hearts were distracted{/idea}.
now: Someone you know well gives you good advice. Your brother. A coworker your age. You think, who is he to tell me? {trap}You dismiss the person to avoid the point.{/trap} {idea}The whisper is usually a distracted heart talking.{/idea}
old: I would listen if the advice came from someone more impressive.
new: When I attack the messenger, my heart is often just avoiding the message.
try: Recall one piece of advice you brushed off because of who said it. Weigh the words alone.

title: Every whisper is heard, in heaven and on earth.
subtitle: The Prophet's calm answer to their secret plotting
then: The Prophet ﷺ did not argue back with insults. He said {idea}my Lord knows what is said in the heavens and on earth{/idea}. The One who knows every secret is the One sending the Quran. For those plotting in private, {trap}this was also a warning{/trap}.
now: The voice note you deleted. The side conversation after the meeting. The thing you said about your in-laws in the car. {trap}It felt private.{/trap} {idea}Nothing said anywhere is unheard.{/idea} That can sting, and it can also comfort when people speak against you.
old: What I say in private stays private.
new: Every word I say has a Hearer. That is a warning and a comfort.
try: Before one private conversation today, remember Allah is listening, and adjust one sentence.

title: Dreams, lies, poetry: they could not settle on one excuse.
subtitle: Changing objections show the problem is not the evidence
then: The Quraysh kept changing their story. Sometimes they called the Quran magic, sometimes poetry, {trap}sometimes mixed-up dreams or a fabrication{/trap}. Then they demanded a sign like the she-camel of Salih or the signs of Musa and 'Isa. The tafsir says their shifting showed {idea}how confused and misguided they were{/idea}.
now: You keep moving the finish line. First you'll start praying once work calms down. Then after the move. Then after the kids are older. {trap}Each excuse replaces the last.{/trap} {idea}When the reasons keep changing, the reason is something else.{/idea}
old: I just have a few questions to settle first.
new: If my reasons keep changing, I should look at what I am really avoiding.
try: Write down the one good thing you keep postponing and every reason you have given. Read the list.

title: Towns before them got their signs and still refused.
subtitle: Why another miracle would not have changed them
then: Answering the demand for a miracle, Allah points to history. The towns that were destroyed {trap}had been given signs and still disbelieved{/trap}. Would these people believe if they saw one? The tafsir notes they had already seen {reward}signs clearer than any earlier nation{/reward}.
now: You tell yourself one more sign would do it. A clear answer to a prayer. A close call on the motorway. But you have had answered prayers, and close calls. {trap}The feeling faded in a week.{/trap} {idea}The problem was never a shortage of signs.{/idea}
old: If Allah showed me something undeniable, I would change.
new: I have already been shown enough. What is missing is my willingness.
try: List three signs of Allah's care you have already seen in your life.

title: Every messenger before him was a man too.
subtitle: Human prophets are a mercy, not a flaw

row.title: one of us
sub: so we can learn from him

then: The objection was that a human could not be a messenger. Allah answers that {idea}every messenger before was a man{/idea}, not an angel. Ask those with earlier scripture, the verse says. The tafsir calls this {reward}part of Allah's perfect blessing{/reward}: messengers from among people, so people could learn from them.
now: You read about a scholar's life and think, they were special, I can't be like that. Or you hear a pious friend lost his temper and feel let down. {idea}Guidance came through people with real lives{/idea} so {reward}you could actually follow it{/reward}.
old: Real guidance should come from someone above ordinary life.
new: Guidance came through humans so that humans could actually live it.
try: Pick one simple habit of the Prophet ﷺ you know of and do it once today.

title: Prophets ate food, and none of them stayed forever.
subtitle: Ordinary needs did not lower their rank
then: The idolaters scoffed that a messenger eats and walks in the markets. Allah replies that {idea}prophets had bodies that ate food{/idea}, earned a living, and died. The tafsir says this {reward}did not reduce their status in any way{/reward}, as the idolaters imagined.
now: You feel your worship is cheapened by the grind. The commute, the shopping, the dishes, the tiredness. {trap}It feels too ordinary to be holy.{/trap} {idea}The best of people lived these same routines.{/idea}
old: My busy, ordinary life keeps me far from anything spiritual.
new: The prophets ate, worked, and shopped. Ordinary life is where faith is lived.
try: Before your next meal, say Bismillah slowly and remember the prophets ate too.

title: The promise was kept: the messengers were saved.
subtitle: Allah's word to His messengers came true
then: Mocked messengers were not left alone. {idea}Allah fulfilled His promise{/idea} to destroy the wrongdoers. He {reward}saved the messengers and their believing followers{/reward}, and the transgressors were destroyed. For the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah, this was a reminder of how such stories end.
now: You stayed honest at work while others cut corners and got promoted. You kept your word while a relative broke theirs and seemed fine. {trap}It looks like they won.{/trap} {idea}Allah has never broken a promise.{/idea}
old: Doing the right thing seems to lose in the end.
new: Allah keeps His promises. The ending is not decided by who looks ahead today.
try: Recall one time a hard right choice paid off later. Thank Allah for it.

title: A Book that carries your honor. Will you not think?
subtitle: The Quran as dignity offered to those who receive it
then: Allah points out {reward}the noble status of the Quran{/reward}. Ibn 'Abbas explained the word as {reward}honor for you{/reward}. The Arabs who opposed it were being offered their own dignity, and asked: {idea}will you not understand this blessing and accept it?{/idea}
now: The Quran sits on the shelf above the TV, wrapped in cloth. You treat it with respect but rarely open it. {idea}It was sent as your honor{/idea}, the thing that would raise you. {trap}Respected from a distance, it cannot.{/trap}
old: The Quran is something I should get around to reading.
new: The Quran is my honor, given to me. Ignoring it is ignoring my own dignity.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page, even slowly, even in translation.

title: Many unjust towns were broken, and others took their place.
subtitle: No people is too big to be replaced
then: The verse reminds the Quraysh of {trap}how many towns given to wrongdoing were destroyed{/trap}. The tafsir stresses that {idea}they were very many{/idea}. After each, Allah raised up another nation that came after them.
now: The company that seemed unshakable is gone. The family name that ruled your town is forgotten. You think your place, your role, your circle will always be there. {idea}Every place gets handed on.{/idea} {reward}What lasts is how you used yours.{/reward}
old: My position feels secure and permanent.
new: Every place I hold will pass to someone else. Only what I did there stays.
try: Think of one role you hold, at home or work. Do one fair thing in it today.

title: When they felt it coming, they ran.
subtitle: Running when the warning finally becomes real
then: These towns had been warned by their prophets. Only {trap}when they realized the punishment would surely come{/trap}, just as warned, did they try to run away. The tafsir describes the moment the warning became something they could feel.
now: The doctor told you two years ago to change your diet. You nodded. Now the results come back and suddenly you are reading every label. {trap}Rushing at the end is common.{/trap} {idea}Moving at the warning is the mercy.{/idea}
old: I will take it seriously when it actually starts happening.
new: The time to act is when I am warned, not when I can feel the consequence.
try: Pick one warning you have been ignoring, about health, money, or faith. Take one step on it today.

title: Go back to your luxuries; you will be asked about them.
subtitle: Comforts become the subject of the question

row.title: a question
sub: how did you thank for it?

then: As they ran, it was said to them, {trap}by way of ridicule{/trap}: do not flee, go back to the luxuries and fine homes you lived in. Qatadah said it was mocking them. They would be questioned, the tafsir says, {idea}about whether they gave thanks for what they had{/idea}.
now: The warm house, the full fridge, the car, the holiday photos. They feel like a place to retreat. {idea}Each one is also a question waiting for you{/idea}: what did you do with it? {reward}Gratitude turns them from questions into answers.{/reward}
old: My comforts are my safe place.
new: My comforts are gifts I will be asked about. Thanks is my answer.
try: Walk through your home and thank Allah out loud for three things in it.

title: Woe to us, we were wrong: said when it no longer helped.
subtitle: A confession that came after the door closed
then: Faced with the punishment, they said the truth at last: {idea}we were wrongdoers{/idea}. The tafsir notes they confessed {trap}when it would be of no benefit to them{/trap}. The words were right. The timing was gone.
now: You know you were wrong in that argument with your sister. You plan to admit it someday. {idea}The same words today are repentance and repair.{/idea} {trap}Left too long, they become only regret.{/trap}
old: I can admit I was wrong later, when it is easier.
new: Admitting wrong is a gift while there is time. Later it may help no one.
try: Say I was wrong, to Allah in prayer and to one person, about one thing today.

title: Their cry went on until they fell silent like harvested fields.
subtitle: The end of the towns that ignored their warnings
then: They kept repeating their admission of wrongdoing until, in the tafsir's words, {trap}their movements and voices came to a stop{/trap}, like a field that has been reaped. The passage closes the story of the destroyed towns. It was told to people in Makkah {idea}who still had time{/idea}.
now: You are not in the field. You are still standing, still breathing, still able to change. {idea}This story was told to people who still had time{/idea}, and so are you. {reward}Today is the gift they did not have.{/reward}
old: Stories of destroyed nations are about other people.
new: These stories are told to me while I still have time to change.
try: Make one sincere istighfar today, naming something specific to Allah.

title: The heavens and earth were not made as a game.
subtitle: Creation has a purpose, and so does your life
then: The surah introduction explains that the Makkan chiefs saw life as {trap}merely sport and pastime{/trap}, with no accountability. Allah answers: He created the heavens and earth {idea}in truth, with justice{/idea}, so that those who do evil and those who do good each receive what they earned.
now: Another weekend of streaming and scrolling, then Monday, then the same again. It can start to feel like life is just filling time. {idea}Nothing around you was made for nothing{/idea}, and {reward}neither were your days{/reward}.
old: Life is mostly about getting through the week and enjoying what I can.
new: The whole universe was made with purpose. My days are part of that purpose.
try: Look at the sky for one minute today and ask what your day is for.

title: Had He wanted a pastime, it would not look like this.
subtitle: A reckoning, a Paradise, a Hell: not the marks of a game

row.title: if a pastime
sub: He would take it from Himself

then: Mujahid explained that if this were a pastime, {idea}Allah would not have created Paradise or Hell, death, resurrection, or the Reckoning{/idea}. Qatadah and others said the verse means {idea}We will not do that{/idea}. A game does not end with an account.
now: You treat a choice as small because nobody seems to be keeping score. The extra change the cashier gave you. The promise you made a child. {trap}It feels like it doesn't matter.{/trap} {idea}A world with a Reckoning is not a world where nothing counts.{/idea}
old: Most of what I do is too small to matter.
new: A world made with a Reckoning is a world where small choices count.
try: Keep one small promise today that you could easily have let slide.

title: Truth is hurled at falsehood, and falsehood is gone.
subtitle: Falsehood looks strong until truth strikes it
then: Allah says He flings the truth against falsehood. The tafsir explains: {idea}We explain the truth and thus defeat falsehood{/idea}, until it is {trap}fading and vanishing{/trap}. The verse then warns those who claimed Allah had offspring about what they invented.
now: A rumour about you spreads through the office. Everyone seems to believe it. You feel you have to shout louder. {idea}A calm, clear truth does more than noise.{/idea} {trap}Lies need constant feeding; truth does not.{/trap}
old: Falsehood is winning because it is louder.
new: When truth is made clear, falsehood has nothing to stand on.
try: Next time you are tempted to argue loudly, state the plain truth once, calmly.

title: Even those near Him are never too proud to worship.
subtitle: Closeness to Allah shows up as humble service
then: Everyone in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. The tafsir says {idea}those near Him are the angels{/idea}. They {reward}do not feel proud or refuse to worship Him{/reward}, and they do not get tired or bored of it.
now: You learn a little, attend a few classes, and start feeling the basics are for beginners. {trap}Pride can hide inside progress.{/trap} {idea}The nearest creatures to Allah never outgrow worship.{/idea}
old: As I grow in knowledge, I need the simple acts less.
new: The closer anyone is to Allah, the more eagerly they serve Him.
try: Do one simple act of worship today with full attention, as if it were new.

title: They glorify Him night and day without slowing down.
subtitle: Constant praise from creatures who never tire
then: The angels {idea}persist in their worship night and day{/idea}, the tafsir says, obeying Allah to the utmost, and they are able to do so. Earlier verses described them as {reward}never weary{/reward}. The whole creation is already praising while people are heedless.
now: While you sleep, while you sit in traffic, while you wait in the clinic, {idea}praise of Allah never stops{/idea}. You cannot match that. {reward}You can join it for a moment{/reward}: a SubhanAllah under your breath at the bus stop.
old: I can never worship enough, so why try to keep it up.
new: Praise of Allah never stops. I can step into it whenever I remember.
try: Say SubhanAllah ten times while waiting somewhere today.

title: Can the gods they made from earth bring anyone back?
subtitle: Testing what we rely on by what it can do
then: Allah asks whether the idols they took from the earth {idea}can bring the dead back to life{/idea}. They cannot do any of that, the tafsir says, {trap}so how can they make them rivals to Allah{/trap} and worship them alongside Him?
now: You lean on your salary, your doctor, your contacts as if they hold your life. They are good things. {trap}None of them can give life or return it.{/trap} {idea}Test what you rely on by what it can actually do.{/idea}
old: As long as I have my job and my savings, I am safe.
new: Only the One who gives life can hold my life. Everything else is a means.
try: Name one thing you lean on too hard. Make dua that Allah bless it, not replace Him.

title: More than one god, and everything would fall apart.
subtitle: The order of the universe points to one Lord
then: Allah says if there were other gods in the heavens and earth, {trap}both would have been ruined{/trap}. The tafsir links it to another verse: each god would take away what he created and {trap}some would try to overcome others{/trap}. {idea}Glorified is Allah{/idea}, far above what they claim.
now: Two managers giving opposite orders. Two parents with different rules. You know how fast things break. {idea}The sunrise arriving on time every morning is a quiet witness to one Lord.{/idea}
old: The order of the world is just how things are.
new: The order of the world is a sign that one Lord runs it.
try: Watch one sunrise or sunset this week and say SubhanAllah at the moment it turns.

title: He is not questioned for what He does. We will be.
subtitle: The difference between the Lord and those He made
then: No one can overturn or object to Allah's rule, the tafsir says, {idea}because of His might, knowledge, wisdom, justice and subtlety{/idea}. But He is the One {trap}who will ask His creation about what they did{/trap}.
now: Something hard happens: a job lost, a test result. You spend nights demanding why. {idea}Asking Allah in dua is good.{/idea} {trap}Putting Him on trial while ignoring your own account is the reverse of how it works.{/trap}
old: Allah owes me an explanation for what happens to me.
new: His wisdom is beyond question. My own deeds are what I will answer for.
try: Turn one why me into a dua today: O Allah, help me through this.

title: Bring your proof. Every message before said the same.
subtitle: Belief in one God is backed by every earlier Book
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}bring your proof{/idea}. This Quran is the Reminder for those with him, and the earlier Books were the Reminder for those before. The tafsir says each was sent with {idea}no god except Allah{/idea}, but {trap}most did not know the truth, so they turned away{/trap}.
now: You hold a belief because your family always has, or because everyone online repeats it. {trap}Ask yourself what your proof is.{/trap} {idea}Faith that has looked at the evidence stands firmer.{/idea}
old: I believe it because that is how I was raised.
new: Belief is stronger when I know why. Truth is not afraid of being asked for proof.
try: Choose one thing you believe and find one reason for it from the Quran.

title: Every messenger carried one message: worship Me alone.
subtitle: The same core call across every prophet
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}every messenger before him was told: there is no god but Me, so worship Me{/idea}. The tafsir adds that {reward}the natural inclination of man, the fitrah, also bears witness to that{/reward}.
now: Your days are pulled in many directions: career, approval, the house, the image. {trap}Each one quietly asks for worship.{/trap} {idea}Every prophet came with the same simple centre{/idea} to bring your life back to one.
old: Faith has so many parts that I lose track of the core.
new: Underneath it all is one message every prophet brought: worship Allah alone.
try: Say La ilaha illa Allah slowly three times today, meaning it.

title: Not children of God, but honored servants.
subtitle: The angels' true status, answering a false claim
then: Some of the Arabs believed {trap}the angels were the daughters of Allah{/trap}. The verse answers: {idea}Glory to Him{/idea}. They are {reward}servants He has honored{/reward}, holding high positions, obeying Him in all their words and deeds.
now: You meet people proud of who they know or which family they come from. You are tempted to feel the same. {idea}The angels' honor comes from serving.{/idea} {reward}Yours can too.{/reward}
old: Status comes from connections and family.
new: The highest honor is being a servant of Allah. Even angels hold that title.
try: Do one act of service for someone today without telling anyone.

title: They never speak before He does; they act on His word.
subtitle: The manners of the angels with their Lord
then: The angels {idea}do not initiate any matter before Allah or go against His commands{/idea}, the tafsir says. On the contrary, {reward}they hasten to do as He commands{/reward}. The verse shows those the idolaters worshipped as obedient servants, not partners.
now: You decide where to work, whom to marry, how to spend the bonus, and then ask if it is halal. {trap}The verdict comes after the decision.{/trap} {idea}The angels wait for His word first.{/idea}
old: I make my decisions, then check if they are acceptable.
new: Look to what Allah says before deciding, not after.
try: Before one decision today, pause and ask what would please Allah here.

title: Even angels intercede only for those He is pleased with.
subtitle: No one can talk you past Allah
then: Allah knows everything before them and behind them. {idea}They cannot intercede except for him with whom He is pleased{/idea}, and they stand {trap}in awe for fear of Him{/trap}. The idolaters hoped their angel-gods would plead for them regardless.
now: You think a pious parent's duas, or a good name in the community, will carry you whatever you do. {trap}Good things, but not a free pass.{/trap} {idea}What matters is being someone Allah is pleased with.{/idea}
old: Someone good will speak up for me in the end.
new: Intercession is for those Allah is pleased with. My work is to seek His pleasure.
try: Ask yourself which one thing you do pleases Allah most. Do it once more today.

title: Any servant claiming godhood would meet Hell.
subtitle: No creature has a share in Allah's place
then: The tafsir calls this {idea}a conditional sentence{/idea}; the condition does not have to take place. The angels do not claim it. The point is that {trap}whoever claims to be a god alongside Allah is a wrongdoer{/trap}, however high their station.
now: You do not claim to be a god. But you may act as the final word at home, or make your own wishes the rule nobody can question. {trap}Small versions of the same claim.{/trap} {idea}No one sits in Allah's place.{/idea}
old: Claims of divinity have nothing to do with me.
new: Whenever I make my will the final word, I should remember who truly has it.
try: Let someone at home decide one thing today that you normally control.

title: Heaven and earth were one, then parted; all life from water.
subtitle: The beginning of creation as a sign of the Creator

row.title: joined
sub: one piece, no rain, no growth

then: Ibn 'Abbas explained that the heavens were joined and gave no rain, and the earth was joined and grew nothing. {idea}Then rain came from the sky and plants from the earth.{/idea} The tafsir says people see creation develop step by step, and {idea}in everything there is a sign of Him{/idea}.
now: You fill a glass from the tap without a thought. You water the plant on the windowsill. You watch a child drink after football. {reward}Every living thing you see began from water.{/reward} {idea}The ordinary is full of signs.{/idea}
old: Water and rain are just part of how the world works.
new: Every drink of water points back to the One who made all life from it.
try: With your next glass of water, drink slowly and say Alhamdulillah after.

title: Mountains keep the ground steady; passes let people find their way.
subtitle: Stability and roads, both placed with care
then: The tafsir says the mountains {reward}stabilize the earth and keep it steady{/reward}, so it does not shake under people. Mountains form barriers between lands, so {idea}Allah created gaps, passes, through them{/idea} so people could travel and be guided.
now: You stand on solid floor every morning without thinking about it. You drive the motorway that cuts through the hills. {idea}Steady ground and a road through are both gifts.{/idea} {reward}When life blocks you, a pass is often already placed.{/reward}
old: Solid ground and open roads are just there.
new: The steadiness under my feet and the way through are both placed for me.
try: On your next journey, notice one road or bridge and thank Allah for the way through.

title: The sky is a guarded roof, and still they look away.
subtitle: Passing by the biggest sign above you
then: Allah made the heaven {reward}like a dome covering the earth, high and protected{/reward}. Yet people {trap}turn away from its signs{/trap}. The tafsir says they do not think about how it was made so vast and high, adorned with bodies moving by night and day.
now: You walk to the car under a full sky and your eyes are on the phone. {trap}Days pass without once looking up.{/trap} {idea}The largest sign of Allah's care is over your head right now.{/idea}
old: The sky is just there; there is nothing new in it.
new: The sky is a roof built and guarded for me. It deserves a look.
try: Step outside tonight and look up at the sky for one full minute.

title: Night, day, sun and moon, each swimming in its orbit.
subtitle: The steady rhythm of time as His creation
then: The tafsir describes night with its darkness and stillness, day with its light and human activity, {idea}sometimes one longer, then they switch{/idea}. Sun and moon each have their own light, path, and term. Ibn 'Abbas said they {reward}revolve like a spinning wheel{/reward}.
now: Your alarm goes off, the sun is up, the bus comes, night falls, you sleep. {trap}It feels like a loop you're stuck in.{/trap} {idea}Each turn is a creation of Allah, running on time{/idea}, and your days are inside that order.
old: Day after day is just a routine to get through.
new: Each day and night is His creation, given to me in order.
try: At sunset today, pause and say a short dua for the night ahead.

title: No one before you lived forever. Will they?
subtitle: Waiting for someone else to die changes nothing
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}no human before him was given immortality in this world{/idea}. His opponents {trap}hoped they would live on after him{/trap}, the tafsir says, but that will not happen; everything will pass away.
now: You wait for a difficult boss to retire, or a rival to move away, as if then life begins. {trap}It is easy to live as if you are the one who stays.{/trap} {idea}You are on the same clock as everyone else.{/idea}
old: Things will be better once certain people are gone.
new: No one stays. My time is as short as theirs, so I use it now.
try: Stop waiting on one person to change. Do one thing today that does not depend on them.

title: Every soul tastes death; hard and easy times are both tests.
subtitle: Good days test you as much as bad ones
then: The tafsir explains: Allah tests people {trap}sometimes with difficulties{/trap} and {reward}sometimes with ease{/reward}, to see who gives thanks and who is ungrateful, who has patience and who despairs. Ibn 'Abbas listed health and sickness, richness and poverty. {idea}Then all return to Him.{/idea}
now: The promotion came through. The scan came back clear. The kids are healthy. You relax and forget to pray on time. {idea}The good stretch is also the exam.{/idea} {reward}Thanks is how you pass it.{/reward}
old: Tests are the hard times. Good times are a break.
new: Ease is as much a test as hardship. Each asks a different thing of me.
try: Name the best thing in your life right now and thank Allah for it in your next prayer.

title: They mocked him for speaking of their gods, yet denied the Merciful.
subtitle: Outrage over idols, indifference to Allah
then: When Abu Jahl and others of Quraysh saw the Prophet ﷺ, they {trap}made fun of him and insulted him{/trap}: is this the one who talks about your gods? The tafsir notes the irony: {idea}they disbelieved in Allah and yet they mocked the Messenger{/idea}.
now: Someone criticises your team, your phone brand, your favourite influencer, and you jump in to defend them. But you scroll past mockery of Allah's name. {trap}What we defend shows what we love.{/trap} {idea}Notice where your loyalty jumps first.{/idea}
old: I just defend what I care about.
new: What I rush to defend shows what holds my heart. Allah should come first.
try: Notice the next thing you rush to defend today. Ask if Allah gets that same care.

title: Man is made of haste. Do not rush Allah.
subtitle: His timing is deliberate, even when you want speed
then: When believers saw the Prophet ﷺ mocked, they {trap}wanted swift vengeance{/trap}. The tafsir says haste is mentioned for this reason. Allah delays, then when He seizes, {idea}He will never let go{/idea}. So He says: I will show you My signs; do not ask Me to hurry.
now: Someone wronged you and seems to be doing fine. You want them exposed this week. You refresh their page. {trap}Haste is in our nature.{/trap} {idea}Allah's timing is not slow; it is exact.{/idea}
old: If justice does not come soon, it is not coming.
new: I am made of haste. Allah is not. His delay is not neglect.
try: Hand one grievance to Allah in dua today and stop checking on it.

title: So when is this promise? they asked, mocking.
subtitle: Asking for the Day as a joke
then: The idolaters tried to hasten the punishment. The tafsir says they did it {trap}out of denial, rejection, stubbornness, and a belief that it will never happen{/trap}. The surah introduction notes they took the lack of punishment so far as proof the warnings were empty.
now: You hear about the Day of Judgement and think, people have said it was near for centuries. {trap}The delay feels like proof it's not real.{/trap} {idea}The delay is the time you have been given.{/idea}
old: If it was coming, it would have come by now.
new: The delay is not evidence against the Day. It is mercy giving me time.
try: Use one minute of today's delay well: make one dua for your own ending.

title: If they only knew, they would not ask to hurry it.
subtitle: Certainty would end the mocking
then: The tafsir explains: {idea}if only they knew for certain that it will inevitably come{/idea}, they would not seek to hasten it. They would {trap}not be able to ward it off and would have no helper{/trap}. Their jokes came from not knowing.
now: You read the warning on the cigarette pack and joke about it. Your friend in the hospital ward does not. {idea}Certainty changes everything.{/idea} {reward}Knowing now, while it can help you, is the gift.{/reward}
old: I know the Day is coming, but it does not feel real.
new: If I were truly certain, I would live differently. Certainty is worth seeking.
try: Read one verse about the Hereafter today slowly, and let it feel real.

title: It will come suddenly, and no one will push it back.
subtitle: No delay once it arrives
then: The tafsir says it will {trap}take them by surprise{/trap}, scare them, and leave them confused. They will have no means to avert it, and {idea}it will not be delayed for them even for an instant{/idea}. The mockers asked when; the answer is: without warning.
now: The call in the middle of the night. The car that didn't stop. {trap}Endings rarely book an appointment.{/trap} {idea}The only preparation that works is the one you start before.{/idea}
old: I will know when it is time to get serious.
new: It comes without notice. The time to get ready is while I have time.
try: Settle one thing you would regret leaving undone: a debt, an apology, a will.

title: Messengers were mocked before you; the mockers met what they mocked.
subtitle: Consolation for the Prophet in his pain
then: Allah {reward}consoles His Messenger ﷺ{/reward} for the pain and insult of the mockery. Messengers before him were mocked, and {trap}the scoffers were surrounded by the punishment they thought would never come{/trap}. Another verse adds that they bore it with patience until help came.
now: Your cousins laugh when you skip the drink at the wedding. A coworker makes a joke about your prayer break. {trap}It stings.{/trap} {reward}Better people than you were laughed at for less, and they were right.{/reward}
old: Being mocked for my faith means I am doing something wrong.
new: The messengers were mocked too. Mockery does not make the truth less true.
try: Next time you are teased for your faith, smile, stay kind, and keep going.

title: Who guards you by night and day but the Most Merciful?
subtitle: The protection you never notice
then: The tafsir speaks of Allah's {reward}favor for His creatures{/reward}: He protects them by night and by day, watching over them with His Eye that never sleeps. Yet {trap}they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord{/trap} and do not recognize His blessings.
now: You lock the door, set the alarm, check the kids are asleep. You drive home on autopilot. {reward}Every safe night is a protection you never saw.{/reward} {idea}Remembering Him is how you notice it.{/idea}
old: I keep myself and my family safe.
new: My care is real, but my safety is from Allah, every hour.
try: Tonight before sleeping, say a short dua placing your family in Allah's care.

title: Their gods cannot even help themselves.
subtitle: The weakness of what people rely on besides Allah
then: Allah asks, in a question meant to rebuke: {trap}do they have gods who can protect them other than Us?{/trap} The tafsir answers: these gods {idea}cannot even help themselves{/idea}, nor can they be guarded from Allah.
now: You count on the bank, the government scheme, the influential uncle. When the market drops or the uncle falls ill, {trap}they cannot save themselves{/trap}. {idea}Lean on what cannot fall.{/idea}
old: With the right backing, I am covered.
new: Anything that cannot protect itself cannot truly protect me. Only Allah can.
try: In one worry today, say Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil before you act.

title: Long comfortable lives fooled them into thinking they were right.
subtitle: Ease that lasts can feel like approval
then: Allah explains that they were {trap}deceived by their luxuries and the long life they had been given{/trap}, so they believed they were following something good. He asks if they do not see the land being reduced from its edges. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said this meant {idea}the victory of Islam over disbelief{/idea}.
now: Business is good, the family is healthy, nothing bad has happened in years. {trap}It is tempting to read that as a sign you're on the right path.{/trap} {idea}Ease is a gift and a respite, not a certificate.{/idea}
old: Things going well for me means I am doing fine with Allah.
new: A long good stretch is a respite to use, not proof that I am right.
try: In a good season, ask yourself one honest question: what am I neglecting while it's easy?

title: I only warn you by revelation, but the deaf hear nothing.
subtitle: A warning works only on ears willing to hear
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say he only conveys {idea}what Allah reveals to him{/idea}. The tafsir says this {trap}is of no benefit to the one whose hearing and heart are sealed{/trap}. The deaf will not hear the call, even when warned.
now: Your mother has told you about the late nights a dozen times. You hear the words and tune them out before she finishes. {trap}That is a kind of deafness.{/trap} {idea}Ears can work while the heart refuses.{/idea}
old: If the message were clearer, I would act on it.
new: Most warnings are clear enough. What matters is whether I let myself hear.
try: Think of one reminder you hear often and tune out. Listen to it fully once today.

title: One whiff of His punishment, and they would confess.
subtitle: How quickly bravado breaks
then: The mockers asked for the punishment boldly. The tafsir says that {trap}if they were touched by even the slightest of it{/trap}, they would confess their sins and admit {idea}they had wronged themselves{/idea}. Their confidence was only skin deep.
now: You are confident about skipping the check-up, until one sharp chest pain at the gym. {trap}Then you promise everything.{/trap} {idea}Better to admit it now, by choice, while it can still change your life.{/idea}
old: I am fine as I am. I don't need to change.
new: My confidence may be thinner than I think. Better to turn back by choice.
try: Admit one fault to Allah today, before anything forces you to.

title: Scales of justice: not even a mustard seed is lost.
subtitle: Every deed is weighed, and no one is wronged
then: Most scholars say it is one Balance, plural to reflect how many deeds are weighed. A companion once told the Prophet ﷺ he hit and insulted his servants. The Prophet ﷺ explained that {trap}any punishment beyond what they deserved would be taken from him{/trap}. The man wept and {reward}set them all free{/reward}.
now: The sharp reply to your child after a long shift. The extra effort no one at work noticed. {idea}Both are on the scale.{/idea} {reward}Two light phrases, SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil 'Azim, are heavy there.{/reward}
old: Small things I do and say don't really count.
new: Even a mustard seed of good or harm will be weighed. Nothing is wasted.
try: Say SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, SubhanAllahil 'Azim ten times today.

title: Musa and Harun were given the Criterion, a light and a reminder.
subtitle: Scripture that separates truth from falsehood

row.title: a light
sub: fills the heart, shows the way

then: The tafsir notes Allah often mentions Musa and Muhammad ﷺ together, and their Books together. Qatadah said the Criterion was the Tawrah, {idea}how Allah differentiated between truth and falsehood{/idea}. The heavenly Books also bring {reward}what fills the heart with light, guidance, and repentance{/reward}.
now: You face a choice at work where everyone says it's fine, and you're not sure. {idea}Guidance is a criterion: it helps you tell right from wrong{/idea} when the crowd blurs it. {reward}And it lights you from inside.{/reward}
old: Scripture is a list of rules to follow.
new: Scripture is a light that helps me see what is true when things blur.
try: Bring one unclear choice to the Quran today. Look up what it says about it.

title: They fear their Lord unseen and are wary of the Hour.
subtitle: Who the reminder actually reaches
then: The verse describes those who benefit from the reminder: they {idea}fear their Lord in the unseen{/idea} and are afraid of the Hour. The tafsir links it to another verse: {reward}theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward{/reward}.
now: The hotel room on a work trip. The browser with no one looking. The office after everyone has gone. {idea}What you do there is what you really believe.{/idea} {reward}That private moment is where forgiveness is earned.{/reward}
old: I behave well because people know me.
new: Real faith shows when no one is watching but Allah.
try: In one private moment today, choose the better thing because only He sees.

title: This is a blessed reminder. Will you deny it?
subtitle: The Quran as blessing, clear and close at hand
then: After Musa's Book, Allah points to the Quran: {reward}a blessed reminder He has sent down{/reward}. The tafsir says falsehood cannot approach it. Then the question: {trap}will you deny it{/trap}, when it is the utmost in clarity and truth?
now: You have an app with the full Quran on your phone, next to forty others you open daily. {trap}Not denying it, exactly. Just not opening it.{/trap} {reward}Blessing sits there waiting.{/reward}
old: I already know what the Quran says, more or less.
new: The Quran is a blessing sent to me. Ignoring it is a quiet kind of denial.
try: Move the Quran app to your home screen and open it once today.

title: Ibrahim was guided early, and Allah knew him well.
subtitle: Guidance given to a young man who was worthy of it
then: Allah {idea}inspired Ibrahim with truth from an early age{/idea}, with proof against his people. The tafsir says {reward}he was worthy of that{/reward}, and Allah was well acquainted with him. The surah now turns to the stories of the prophets.
now: Your teenager asks hard questions about God over dinner. You think, they're too young to get it. {idea}Ibrahim saw clearly as a young man.{/idea} {reward}Young hearts can be the most honest.{/reward}
old: Serious faith is for when you are older.
new: Guidance can come early. Allah knows who is ready for it.
try: Ask a young person in your family what they think about Allah, and listen.

title: What are these statues you sit so devoted to?
subtitle: A young man questioning what everyone takes for granted
then: This was the guidance Ibrahim had in his youth: {idea}his denunciation of his people's worship of idols{/idea} instead of Allah. He asked his own father and people {trap}what these images were that they worshipped with such devotion{/trap}.
now: Look at what your family gives hours to: the TV schedule, the status, what the neighbours think. {trap}Some things get devotion just because they are always there.{/trap} {idea}A simple question can break the spell.{/idea}
old: Everyone around me is devoted to these things, so they must matter.
new: Devotion should have a reason. It is fair to ask what I am devoted to.
try: Ask yourself: what got most of my attention this week? Is it worth that?

title: Their only answer: our fathers did it.
subtitle: Tradition offered in place of evidence
then: Asked what the idols were, his people answered: {trap}we found our fathers worshipping them{/trap}. The tafsir notes {idea}they had no other evidence{/idea} apart from the misguided actions of their forefathers.
now: We have always done the wedding this way. We always shout in arguments. We always keep money matters secret. {trap}Always is not a reason.{/trap} {idea}Keep what is good; question what is only habit.{/idea}
old: This is how my family has always done it.
new: That something was inherited does not make it right. I can check it.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly whether it pleases Allah.

title: You and your fathers were plainly wrong.
subtitle: Error does not become right with age
then: Ibrahim answered that speaking to their fathers {idea}would be the same as speaking to them{/idea}. The tafsir paraphrases: {trap}both you and they are misguided{/trap} and not on any straight path. Pointing to the past did not move the question.
now: You love your grandparents. You also know one of their habits was unfair to someone. {idea}You can honour people and still not repeat their mistake.{/idea} {reward}That is often the kindest thing for the next generation.{/reward}
old: Saying my elders were wrong would be disrespectful.
new: I can respect those before me and still say a wrong was wrong.
try: Choose one inherited mistake you will not pass on, and make dua for the ones before you.

title: Are you serious, or just playing?
subtitle: When the truth is so unfamiliar it sounds like a joke
then: When Ibrahim questioned their intelligence and belittled their gods, they asked: {trap}are you speaking in jest or telling the truth?{/trap} The tafsir adds their reason: {idea}we have never heard such a thing before{/idea}.
now: A friend suggests you give up the extra job and spend evenings with your kids. {trap}It sounds ridiculous because no one you know does it.{/trap} {idea}Unfamiliar is not the same as wrong.{/idea}
old: If I have never heard it before, it is probably not serious.
new: Truth can sound strange just because I have not heard it. That is not a reason to laugh it off.
try: Take one idea you dismissed as strange this week and think about it seriously for five minutes.

title: Your Lord made the heavens and earth, and I bear witness.
subtitle: Ibrahim's clear answer: the Creator is the Lord
then: Ibrahim was not joking. He said {idea}your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them{/idea}. The tafsir adds that He initiated their creation and is the Creator of all things. And Ibrahim said: {reward}I bear witness{/reward} that there is no god other than Him.
now: Someone at the table asks, half laughing, if you actually believe all this. You can mumble, or you can say plainly what you believe, kindly. {reward}Ibrahim simply testified.{/reward}
old: I keep my beliefs quiet so no one thinks I am strange.
new: I can calmly say what I believe. The Creator is my Lord, and I testify to it.
try: If faith comes up in conversation today, say one clear, kind sentence about what you believe.

title: By Allah, I will deal with your idols once you leave.
subtitle: A resolve made openly, before the festival
then: Ibrahim swore an oath, {idea}which some of his people heard{/idea}, to break their idols after they went out to their festival. Ibn Mas'ud reported that when they passed him on the way and asked if he was coming, {trap}he said, I am sick{/trap}.
now: You have talked for months about clearing the haram subscriptions off your phone, or the habit you hate. {trap}Talk has become the whole plan.{/trap} {idea}Ibrahim set a time and followed through.{/idea}
old: Saying I disapprove is enough.
new: Conviction becomes real when I decide when and how I will act.
try: Pick one bad habit and name the exact time today you will remove it.

title: He broke them all, but left the biggest standing.
subtitle: A question set up for the people to face
then: Ibrahim {trap}smashed all the idols except the biggest{/trap}. It was said he put the hammer in its hands, so people would wonder if it had broken the rest. The aim was {idea}that they might turn to it{/idea} and see for themselves.
now: Your friend insists a lucky charm or a horoscope app runs her week. You could mock it. {idea}A good question that lets her see it herself{/idea} often works better than a lecture.
old: To change someone's mind, I need to win the argument.
new: Sometimes the best move is to set up a question they answer themselves.
try: In one disagreement today, ask a sincere question instead of making a point.

title: Who did this to our gods? Gods who could not protect themselves.
subtitle: The scene that should have opened their eyes
then: They returned and saw what Ibrahim had done, {trap}humiliating their idols{/trap} and lowering their status. The tafsir says it was {idea}proof they were not divine{/idea}. Still, their first thought was to find and blame the one who did it.
now: Your plan built on that one investment collapses. Your first instinct is to find who to blame. {idea}The better question is why you trusted something that couldn't hold.{/idea}
old: When something I relied on fails, I look for who is at fault.
new: When something I relied on falls, I should ask why I relied on it.
try: Think of one thing that let you down recently. Ask what it shows about where your trust was.

title: We heard a young man named Ibrahim speak of them.
subtitle: One young voice remembered in a whole town
then: Those who had heard his oath said: {idea}we heard a young man talking about them, called Ibrahim{/idea}. He was alone against the whole town's religion. {reward}His words had been noticed{/reward} even before the idols fell.
now: You are the only one in the office who doesn't join the gossip, the only one in the friend group who prays. {trap}You feel invisible.{/trap} {reward}People notice more than you think.{/reward}
old: I'm one person. What I stand for goes unnoticed.
new: One young voice stood against a whole town. People notice what I stand for.
try: Do one small right thing today in front of others, without fuss.

title: Bring him before everyone, they said. That was his aim.
subtitle: Their trial became his stage
then: They wanted him {trap}brought before a large audience{/trap} as witnesses. The tafsir says {idea}this was Ibrahim's ultimate purpose{/idea}: to tell the whole gathering how foolish it was to worship idols that could not defend themselves.
now: You are called into the meeting to explain why you refused to sign off the false figures. It feels like being put on trial. {reward}It may also be the moment everyone hears why honesty matters.{/reward}
old: Being put on the spot is the worst thing that can happen.
new: The moment they put me on the spot can be the moment truth gets heard.
try: If you are challenged on something right today, answer calmly and clearly.

title: Was it you who did this to our gods, Ibrahim?
subtitle: The question at the centre of the gathering
then: Before everyone, they asked: {trap}are you the one who did this to our gods, O Ibrahim?{/trap} They thought he was on trial. {idea}In truth, their gods were{/idea}, broken and unable to say a word.
now: Your family questions why you stopped joining in a habit you all shared. {trap}You feel you are the one being judged.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the question you are asked puts the old habit on trial instead.{/idea}
old: When I am questioned, I am the one on trial.
new: When I am questioned for doing right, the wrong is what is really on trial.
try: If someone questions your faith choices today, answer with one honest sentence, not defensively.

title: The big one did it. Ask them, if they can speak.
subtitle: A reply that made the idols answer for themselves
then: Ibrahim pointed to the idol he had left whole: {idea}ask them, if they can speak!{/idea} The tafsir says he hoped {reward}they would admit of their own will{/reward} that the idols could not speak, because they were lifeless.
now: You keep checking the stock app or the follower count as if it will tell you you're okay. {trap}Ask it anything that matters. It says nothing.{/trap} {idea}What cannot answer you cannot guide you.{/idea}
old: The things I check for reassurance tell me how I am doing.
new: What cannot speak, hear, or answer cannot be what I turn to.
try: Next time you reach for something for reassurance, make a short dua instead.

title: For a moment they turned on themselves: we are the wrongdoers.
subtitle: A flash of self-blame, aimed at the wrong thing
then: The tafsir explains they {trap}blamed themselves for not protecting their gods{/trap}: you are the wrongdoers because you neglected them. {idea}They came close to the point and missed it.{/idea} A god that needs guarding is no god.
now: The diet failed, so you blame yourself for not trying hard enough, then try the same fad again. {trap}You fix the details and keep the bad idea.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the plan itself is what needs dropping.{/idea}
old: When something fails, I just need to try harder at it.
new: Sometimes the failure is not my effort but the thing I put my trust in.
try: Look at one repeated failure in your life and ask whether the goal itself is wrong.

title: Heads down, they admitted: you know these cannot speak.
subtitle: The truth spoken, and then turned away from
then: The tafsir says {trap}they looked at the ground{/trap}. Qatadah said they admitted their guilt and confusion: {idea}you know well these do not speak{/idea}, so how can you tell us to ask them? They had said the truth out loud.
now: You admit to your spouse that the phone at dinner is a problem. You both nod. {trap}Next evening, same thing.{/trap} {idea}Saying the truth is the first step, not the last.{/idea}
old: Admitting I'm wrong is the hard part, and I've done it.
new: Admitting the truth only helps if I let it change what I do.
try: Take one thing you have already admitted is wrong, and change one detail of it today.

title: Then why worship what cannot help you or harm you?
subtitle: Ibrahim draws the conclusion from their own words
then: Once they admitted it, Ibrahim said: if they cannot speak, {trap}and can neither benefit nor harm you{/trap}, {idea}why do you worship them instead of Allah?{/idea} He used their own answer to make the case.
now: You feel anxious if you miss your morning ritual of checking the news, or that good-luck routine before an interview. {trap}It neither helps nor hurts.{/trap} {idea}Your hope belongs with the One who actually can.{/idea}
old: Some of my habits keep things going well for me.
new: If something cannot help or harm me, it does not deserve my hope or fear.
try: Replace one superstitious habit today with Bismillah and a short dua.

title: Shame on you and your idols. Will you not think?
subtitle: The argument ends with a call to reason
then: Ibrahim asked if they did not realize {trap}the extent of the misguidance they were following{/trap}. The tafsir says {idea}he defeated them in argument and left them with no way out{/idea}. Allah calls it the proof He gave Ibrahim against his people.
now: You know the facts about your spending, your sleep, your screen time. {trap}You just never sit down and think them through.{/trap} {idea}Faith asks you to use the mind you were given.{/idea}
old: Thinking too hard about my life only makes me anxious.
new: Allah asks me to think. Clear thinking leads me back to Him.
try: Sit for five minutes today and honestly think through one habit and where it leads.

title: Out of arguments, they shouted: burn him, defend your gods.
subtitle: When reasoning fails, force takes over
then: When {trap}their arguments were refuted and falsehood defeated{/trap}, they turned to power and said: burn him. They gathered a huge amount of wood. Ibn 'Abbas reported that as Ibrahim was thrown, he said {reward}Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs{/reward}.
now: You make a fair point in the family argument and someone starts shouting or threatening. {trap}Volume rises when reasons run out.{/trap} {reward}Ibrahim's words fit that moment too: Allah is enough for me.{/reward}
old: When I am losing an argument, I need to push harder.
new: When I run out of reasons, I should stop, not get louder. Allah is enough.
try: When you feel cornered today, say Hasbiyallahu wa ni'mal wakil and lower your voice.

title: O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim.
subtitle: Allah's command over the thing meant to destroy
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the angel of rain asked when he would be told to send rain, but {idea}Allah's command was swifter{/idea}: O fire, be coolness and safety. Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Al-'Aliyah said that without the word {reward}safety{/reward}, Ibrahim would have been harmed by the cold.
now: The redundancy letter, the diagnosis, the court date. {trap}It looks like fire.{/trap} {idea}The same Lord who spoke to Ibrahim's fire is your Lord.{/idea} {reward}He can make the hard thing safe for you.{/reward}
old: Some situations are simply too dangerous to come through.
new: Nothing harms except by Allah's leave. He can make the fire safe.
try: Name the thing you fear most right now, and ask Allah to make it cool and safe for you.

title: They plotted to harm him, and became the greatest losers.
subtitle: A plot against a prophet turned on the plotters
then: They {trap}wanted to plot against the Prophet of Allah{/trap}, the tafsir says, {idea}but Allah planned against them and saved him from the fire{/idea}. They were defeated and humiliated. The whole town lost to one young man who relied on Allah.
now: Someone at work is quietly trying to get you pushed out. You are tempted to plot back. {idea}Stay honest, do your work, rely on Allah.{/idea} {reward}His plan outlasts theirs.{/reward}
old: If someone plots against me, I have to out-plot them.
new: Allah's plan outlasts every plot. My job is to stay upright and rely on Him.
try: Instead of planning a comeback against someone, make dua for your own protection and their guidance.

title: Saved from the fire, Ibrahim and Lut reach a blessed land.
subtitle: Leaving a hostile home for a place of blessing
then: Allah saved Ibrahim from the fire his people lit and {idea}brought him out from among them{/idea}, migrating to the land of Ash-Sham. Lut, who believed in him, went with him. Allah calls it {reward}the land We blessed for the worlds{/reward}.
now: You left the job, the city, or the friend group because staying meant compromising your faith. {trap}It felt like losing everything.{/trap} {reward}Allah can bring you somewhere better than what you left.{/reward}
old: Walking away from a bad place means I end up with less.
new: When I leave something for Allah, He can bring me to something blessed.
try: Thank Allah for one thing you gained after leaving something behind.

title: He asked for one son and was given a grandson too.
subtitle: Ishaq, and Ya'qub as an extra gift
then: Ibrahim had prayed, {idea}my Lord, grant me a righteous son{/idea}. 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd said Allah gave him Ishaq, {reward}and Ya'qub in addition{/reward}. Mujahid said nafilah means a gift. Allah made each of them righteous.
now: You prayed for one job offer and got two. You asked for your child to pass, and he also found good friends. {reward}Allah's answers often come with something extra.{/reward} {idea}Notice the extra.{/idea}
old: I am lucky if Allah gives me exactly what I asked for.
new: Allah answers generously, often with more than I asked.
try: Remember one dua answered with something extra, and thank Allah for the extra.

title: Leaders who guided, prayed, gave, and lived what they taught.
subtitle: Leadership measured by doing good and worship
then: Allah made them {idea}leaders, examples to be followed{/idea}, inviting to Him by His leave. He inspired them to good deeds, prayer, and zakah. The tafsir says {reward}they did what they enjoined others to do{/reward}.
now: At home you tell the kids to put their phones away at dinner while yours is in your hand. {trap}They learn from what you do.{/trap} {idea}You lead your family by living it first.{/idea}
old: Leading means telling others what to do.
new: Real leaders live first what they ask of others.
try: Pick one thing you ask your family to do, and do it yourself today, visibly.

title: Lut was given wisdom and saved from a town of evil.
subtitle: A prophet kept safe among rebellious people
then: Lut believed in Ibrahim, followed him, and migrated with him. Allah {reward}gave him wisdom and knowledge{/reward}, made him a prophet, and sent him to Sodom and its area. {trap}They rejected him{/trap}, and Allah saved him from the town that practised wicked deeds.
now: Your workplace, your building, your online space may make wrong things normal. {trap}It is easy to drift with the place.{/trap} {idea}Lut lived among them and did not become them.{/idea}
old: I am bound to pick up the ways of the place I live.
new: I can live among people and still hold to what is right, with Allah's help.
try: Name one wrong habit normal in your surroundings, and quietly decline it today.

title: Lut was taken into His mercy: one of the righteous.
subtitle: What remains after the town is gone
then: After the story of Lut's people, the verse closes on him: {reward}We admitted him to Our mercy{/reward}. {idea}He was of the righteous.{/idea} The town is not the last word in his story. Mercy is.
now: You feel alone being the one who doesn't laugh at the cruel joke or join the shady deal. {trap}It feels like losing.{/trap} {reward}The last word on the righteous is mercy.{/reward}
old: Standing apart from everyone leaves me with nothing.
new: The righteous end up inside Allah's mercy, even if they stood alone.
try: Ask Allah today: admit me into Your mercy among the righteous.

title: Nuh called out, and he and his family were saved.
subtitle: A dua after centuries of patience
then: Nuh {idea}remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty{/idea}, calling them to Allah, and only a few believed. They plotted against him generation after generation. Then he called on his Lord: I am overcome, so help me. {reward}Allah answered and saved him and those who believed{/reward} from the great distress.
now: You've been trying for years: with a hard relative, a long illness, a child who has drifted. {trap}You feel you have nothing left.{/trap} {idea}Nuh's patience ran for centuries, and then he asked for help.{/idea} {reward}He was answered.{/reward}
old: I have been patient long enough; nothing is changing.
new: Patience and dua go together. Allah answers the one who keeps calling.
try: Make a short, honest dua today: my Lord, I am worn out, so help me.

title: Helped against those who denied, and they were drowned.
subtitle: The end of a people who rejected every sign
then: Allah {reward}saved Nuh and helped him{/reward} against the people who denied His signs. {trap}They were a people given to evil, and Allah drowned them all{/trap}, as their prophet had prayed. The story was told to Makkans who were also mocking a prophet.
now: You are in the minority at the office, at family gatherings, maybe even among friends, on something you know is right. {trap}Numbers feel like proof.{/trap} {idea}Nuh had a few with him, and they were the ones saved.{/idea}
old: If most people disagree with me, I am probably wrong.
new: Numbers do not decide the truth. The few with Nuh were the ones saved.
try: Hold to one right thing today even if you are the only one doing it.

title: Dawud and Sulayman judged the vineyard ruined by sheep at night.
subtitle: Two prophets, one case, and Allah witnessing
then: Ibn Mas'ud said the field was a vineyard whose bunches were spoiled by sheep. {idea}Dawud ruled that the owner of the vineyard should keep the sheep.{/idea} Sulayman proposed another way. Allah says {reward}We were witness to their judgement{/reward}.
now: Your kids fight over a broken toy. Two coworkers bring you a dispute. {trap}You decide quickly to end the noise.{/trap} {idea}Every decision you make between people is witnessed by Allah.{/idea}
old: Sorting out disputes is just about ending the argument.
new: When I judge between people, Allah is witness. Fairness matters, even in small cases.
try: In the next small dispute you settle, listen to both sides fully before deciding.

title: Sulayman was given understanding; both were given wisdom.
subtitle: One saw further, and neither was blamed
then: Sulayman suggested the shepherd tend the vines until they grew back, while the vineyard owner benefited from the sheep, then {reward}each would get his own back{/reward}. Al-Hasan noted that {idea}Allah praised Sulayman but did not condemn Dawud{/idea}. The mountains and birds glorified Allah with Dawud's beautiful recitation.
now: Your colleague's idea turns out better than yours. {trap}You feel small.{/trap} {idea}Sincere effort is honoured even when someone else sees further.{/idea} {reward}Learn from it, without shame.{/reward}
old: If my judgment turns out wrong, I have failed.
new: Sincere effort is honoured. I can learn from a better answer without shame.
try: Tell someone today that their idea was better than yours, and mean it.

title: Dawud was taught to make armor. Will you be grateful?
subtitle: A skill taught by Allah, for people's protection
then: Qatadah said people used to wear plated armor, and Dawud {reward}was the first to make rings of chain mail{/reward}. The tafsir says Allah blessed people when He inspired His servant Dawud and taught him this for their sake. {idea}Are you then grateful?{/idea}
now: You are good at code, at nursing, at fixing cars, at calming a crying baby. {trap}It feels like it is just you.{/trap} {reward}Every skill is something Allah taught{/reward}, and it is meant to protect and help others.
old: My skills are mine; I earned them.
new: My skills were taught to me by Allah. Gratitude is using them for good.
try: Use one of your skills today to help someone, for free.

title: The strong wind ran at Sulayman's command, by Allah's leave.
subtitle: Power over nature, given and known by Allah
then: The tafsir introduces this as {reward}the unparalleled power of Sulayman{/reward}: Allah subjugated the strong wind to him, running by his command toward the land Allah had blessed. The verse ends: {idea}of all things We are Knowing{/idea}.
now: You have power you take for granted: a car, a salary, a team that answers to you. {trap}It can start to feel like yours.{/trap} {idea}Every bit of control you have is lent, and Allah knows how you use it.{/idea}
old: The control I have over my life is my own doing.
new: Any power I hold is subjected to me by Allah, and He knows how I use it.
try: Use one bit of authority you have today more gently than usual.

title: Even devils worked for Sulayman, and Allah kept them in check.
subtitle: No force works outside Allah's guard
then: Among the devils were some {idea}who dived for Sulayman and did other work{/idea}. Allah says {reward}it was We who guarded them{/reward}. Even the most rebellious creatures worked only within His control.
now: You feel at the mercy of things you can't see: whispers, bad luck, other people's envy. {trap}Fear can make them feel huge.{/trap} {idea}Nothing in the unseen works outside Allah's guard.{/idea}
old: There are dark forces out there I cannot do anything about.
new: Even the devils are under Allah's control. I seek refuge in Him and move on.
try: Recite Ayat al-Kursi tonight before sleep, and leave the fear with Allah.

title: Ayyub said: harm has touched me, and You are most merciful.
subtitle: A dua that names the pain and the mercy
then: Ayyub had livestock, crops, many children and fine houses, and {trap}lost them all{/trap}. Then his body was tested, and only his wife cared for him. The Prophet ﷺ said the prophets are tested most severely. Ayyub {reward}had the utmost patience{/reward}, and his dua names only the harm and Allah's mercy.
now: Lying awake in the hospital bed, or after the business went under, you want to ask why me. {idea}Ayyub simply told Allah it hurt, and called Him the Most Merciful.{/idea} {reward}That is patience and honesty together.{/reward}
old: Being patient means never saying it hurts.
new: I can tell Allah it hurts and still call Him the Most Merciful. That is patience.
try: In your next dua, tell Allah plainly what hurts, then call Him Arham ar-Rahimin.

title: He was answered: healed, his family restored, and as many again.
subtitle: Ayyub's story as a reminder for anyone tested
then: Allah removed his distress and {reward}restored his family and the like of them{/reward}, as a mercy. The tafsir says Allah made him an example {idea}lest those beset by trials think it is because He does not care for them{/idea}. When healed, Ayyub said: who can ever have enough of Your mercy?
now: A long hard year makes you wonder if Allah has forgotten you. {trap}That thought is exactly what this story answers.{/trap} {idea}Ayyub's test was a sign of his rank, and it ended in mercy.{/idea}
old: If I am being tested this hard, Allah must not care about me.
new: Trials are not a sign that Allah doesn't care. Ayyub's ended in mercy.
try: Write down one hard time that ended. Read it the next time you feel forgotten.

title: Isma'il, Idris, Dhul-Kifl: each of them was patient.
subtitle: Three names joined by one quality
then: Isma'il was the son of Ibrahim, and Idris was mentioned in Surah Maryam. Of Dhul-Kifl, the tafsir says {idea}the context suggests he was a prophet{/idea}; others said he was a righteous man and a just judge, and Ibn Jarir made no firm comment. {reward}What the verse records about all three is patience.{/reward}
now: Few people will know your name in a hundred years. Your job title won't matter. {idea}What lasts is a word like patient{/idea}: the parent who stayed calm, the carer who kept going. {reward}That is a legacy.{/reward}
old: To be remembered, I need to do something big.
new: Allah remembered these prophets with one word: patient. That can be my legacy too.
try: Choose one situation today where you will be patient on purpose.

title: Admitted into His mercy, for they were righteous.
subtitle: Where patience leads
then: Right after naming Isma'il, Idris and Dhul-Kifl as patient, Allah says {reward}We admitted them to Our mercy{/reward}. {idea}They were of the righteous.{/idea} The same words were said of Lut a few verses earlier.
now: You hold your tongue through the in-law's comments for the hundredth time. {trap}It feels like it goes nowhere.{/trap} {reward}Patience that is for Allah ends inside His mercy.{/reward}
old: Being patient just means putting up with things.
new: Patience for Allah's sake is a road into His mercy.
try: When you hold back a sharp word today, quietly ask Allah to count it for you.

title: In three darknesses, Yunus said: none but You, I was wrong.
subtitle: The prayer from inside the whale

key.label: What he did in the dark

then: Yunus {trap}left his people in anger{/trap} and boarded a ship; the lot fell on him and he was swallowed by a great fish. Ibn Mas'ud said the darknesses were {trap}the belly of the fish, the sea, and the night{/trap}. There he called: {idea}there is no god but You, glory be to You, I was of the wrongdoers{/idea}.
now: Stuck in the dark: the debt you can't see out of, the 3 a.m. panic, the mistake that cost you. {idea}Yunus didn't argue or blame.{/idea} He glorified Allah and owned his part. {reward}That prayer works from any darkness.{/reward}
old: When I am in a hole, the first thing is to work out who caused it.
new: In the dark, I turn to Allah, praise Him, and own my part.
try: Say the dua of Yunus three times today: La ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.

title: We answered him and saved him. So We save the believers.
subtitle: A promise that reaches past Yunus to you
then: Allah {reward}brought him out of the fish and the darkness{/reward}. The tafsir says {idea}this is how He saves believers{/idea} who call on Him in difficulty and repent, especially with these words. Sa'd reported the Prophet ﷺ said that no Muslim prays with them for anything except that He answers.
now: You think the story of Yunus is about a prophet, a whale, a long time ago. {idea}The last line is about you.{/idea} {reward}The same rescue is promised to anyone who calls the same way.{/reward}
old: Miracles of rescue happened to prophets, not to people like me.
new: Allah says He saves believers the way He saved Yunus. That promise includes me.
try: Make the dua of Yunus for one specific difficulty you are in right now.

title: Zakariyya prayed: do not leave me alone; You are the best heir.
subtitle: A quiet dua with praise woven in
then: Zakariyya {idea}cried to his Lord in secret, hiding it from his people{/idea}. He asked not to be left with no heir to stand among the people after him. The tafsir calls his closing words, {reward}You are the best of inheritors{/reward}, a praise befitting the request.
now: You want a child, or a spouse, or someone to carry on your work, and you feel embarrassed to keep asking. {idea}Zakariyya asked quietly, in old age{/idea}, and praised Allah with a name that fit his need.
old: Some wishes are too late or too private to keep asking for.
new: I can ask quietly, at any age, and praise Allah with the name that fits my need.
try: Make a private dua tonight, and end it with a name of Allah that fits what you asked.

title: They rushed to good, called in hope and fear, and were humble.
subtitle: The family whose dua was answered with Yahya
then: Allah gave Zakariyya Yahya and {reward}cured his wife{/reward}, who had been barren. Then He describes them: they {idea}hastened to good deeds{/idea}, called on Him in hope and fear, and were humble. Abu Sinan said khushu' is {idea}the fear that should never leave our hearts{/idea}.
now: You plan to start the good deed when things calm down: the volunteering, the extra prayer, the visit to your aunt. {trap}They never calm down.{/trap} {idea}The ones Allah praised rushed to good.{/idea}
old: I will do more good when I have more time.
new: The people Allah praised rushed to good, with hope and fear and humility.
try: Do the good deed you have been postponing today, even in a small form.

title: Maryam guarded her chastity; she and her son became a sign.
subtitle: A wonder even greater than Zakariyya's
then: Zakariyya's story, a child to an old man and barren wife, comes first because the two are connected. Then comes Maryam's, {idea}even more wondrous{/idea}: a child born without a father. The tafsir says she and her son are {reward}evidence that Allah is able to do all things{/reward}.
now: Doctors gave you the odds. The bank said no. Your situation looks closed by every normal rule. {idea}Allah's power is not bound by the odds.{/idea} {reward}Keep your own purity, and leave the impossible to Him.{/reward}
old: Some outcomes are simply impossible in my situation.
new: Allah creates what He wills. My part is to stay upright, like Maryam.
try: Make one dua today for something you had written off as impossible.

title: Your religion is one religion, and I am your Lord.
subtitle: All the prophets just named stood on one path
then: After the long list of prophets, Allah says: {idea}your religion is one religion{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}we prophets are brothers from different mothers, and our religion is one{/reward}. They all worshipped Allah alone, though their laws differed.
now: You read about Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Yunus, Maryam, 'Isa. {idea}They are not distant strangers. They are your spiritual family{/idea}, all calling to the same Lord you pray to. {reward}You belong to a long line.{/reward}
old: The prophets of the past belong to different stories.
new: All the prophets brought one religion. I stand in their line when I worship Allah.
try: Read the story of one prophet from this surah again and notice what you share.

title: People split apart, but every one of them returns to Us.
subtitle: Division on earth, one return to Allah
then: The nations {trap}were divided over their messengers{/trap}: some believed and some rejected. Allah says {idea}they all shall return to Us{/idea}. On the Day of Resurrection, the tafsir says, each person will be repaid according to his own deeds.
now: The family WhatsApp group splits over an argument. The mosque committee divides. {trap}You spend energy proving you're right.{/trap} {idea}Everyone is heading to the same return, where your own deeds are what count.{/idea}
old: Settling who is right in every dispute matters most.
new: We all return to Allah. My own deeds matter more than winning the argument.
try: Step out of one argument today and spend that energy on a good deed.

title: Good done with faith is never rejected. We write it down.
subtitle: No sincere effort is wasted
then: Whoever does good while believing, {idea}his heart believes and his deeds are righteous{/idea}, the tafsir says. {reward}His efforts will not be wasted{/reward}; they will be appreciated, without a speck of injustice. All his deeds are recorded, and nothing is lost.
now: The night feeds no one thanked you for. The report your boss took credit for. The care for a parent who no longer recognises you. {trap}It feels invisible.{/trap} {reward}It is written down.{/reward}
old: If nobody notices what I do, it doesn't really count.
new: Every good I do with faith is recorded. None of it is lost.
try: Do one unseen good deed today and tell no one.

title: A destroyed town will not come back for a second chance.
subtitle: This life is the only time to act
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the ban is enforced: {trap}it has been decreed that the people of each destroyed town will never return to this world{/trap} before the Day of Resurrection. {idea}There is no going back to fix it.{/idea}
now: Games have restart buttons. Phones have undo. {trap}Life does not.{/trap} {idea}This day, this family, this chance to make things right, is the one you get.{/idea}
old: There will always be another chance to get it right.
new: No one comes back to redo their life. Today is the chance.
try: Do one thing today you would want done if you had no tomorrow.

title: Until Ya'juj and Ma'juj are let loose, rushing from every height.
subtitle: A sign of the end, told by the One who knows
then: The tafsir says they will {trap}come forth quickly to spread corruption{/trap}, rushing down from every raised piece of land, described {idea}as if the listener can see it{/idea}. This is information from the One who knows what has happened and what is to come.
now: Endless videos online claim to decode the end times. {trap}It is easy to get lost in speculation.{/trap} {idea}What Allah tells you about the end is a reminder to get ready, not a puzzle.{/idea}
old: Knowing the signs of the end is about predicting when.
new: The signs are told so I prepare, not so I speculate.
try: Skip one end-times video today and spend those minutes in dhikr.

title: The true promise arrives: we were heedless, we were wrong.
subtitle: The same confession the surah opened with
then: The surah began: {trap}the reckoning is near, yet they are heedless{/trap}. Here the deniers say it themselves: woe to us, we were heedless of this. Then they correct themselves: {idea}no, we were wrongdoers{/idea}. Heedlessness had been a choice.
now: You tell yourself you are just busy, just distracted, not bad. {trap}Busy can be a polite word for choosing not to look.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to name it now, while it can still change.{/idea}
old: I am not doing wrong, I am just busy and distracted.
new: Staying heedless is a choice. I would rather notice now than say it then.
try: Name one thing you've been too busy for that matters to Allah. Give it ten minutes today.

title: You and what you worship besides Allah fuel the Fire.
subtitle: False gods end up where their worshippers do
then: Allah addressed the idolaters of Quraysh: {trap}you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell{/trap}. Ibn 'Abbas said the word means kindling. Ibn Ishaq reported the Prophet ﷺ recited this in the Masjid after {idea}defeating An-Nadr bin Al-Harith in argument{/idea}.
now: Whatever you make the centre of your life in place of Allah: money, status, a person's approval. {trap}It cannot save you; it will not even save itself.{/trap} {idea}Put Allah back in the centre while you can.{/idea}
old: What I put at the centre of my life will look after me.
new: Anything I worship besides Allah will fail with me. Only He can save.
try: Ask: what do I fear losing more than Allah's pleasure? Make dua to put it in its place.

title: Had they been gods, they would not have gone in.
subtitle: The final proof against false gods
