then: The tafsir explains: {idea}if these idols had really been gods, they would not have entered the Fire{/idea}. Their end is the proof of what they were. The worshippers and what they worshipped {trap}remain there together{/trap}.
now: That thing you trust to keep you safe, a career or a reputation, can be damaged by one bad week. {trap}If it can be harmed, it cannot be your god.{/trap} {idea}Only Allah is beyond all harm.{/idea}
old: What I rely on seems strong enough to keep me safe.
new: Anything that can be harmed cannot be my real refuge. Only Allah is beyond harm.
try: Notice one thing you treat as unbreakable today, and remember it can fail.

title: Deep sighing there, and no hearing.
subtitle: Those who refused to listen, unable to hear
then: The tafsir links the sighing to another verse about the people of the Fire. The verse adds that {trap}therein they will hear not{/trap}. In this life they {idea}listened to revelation while they played{/idea}, as the surah's opening said.
now: Every day you can hear the adhan, a reminder, a friend's honest advice. {reward}Hearing is a gift you have right now.{/reward} {idea}Use it while it can still change something.{/idea}
old: I can always tune in to reminders later.
new: Being able to hear guidance is a gift. I should use it now.
try: When you hear the next adhan, stop what you are doing and listen to it all.

title: Those already promised the best are kept far from it.
subtitle: Mercy that went ahead of the righteous
then: Ibn Az-Zab'ari argued that if all worshipped besides Allah go to the Fire, then so would the angels, 'Uzayr and 'Isa. The Prophet ﷺ answered that whoever likes to be worshipped instead of Allah will be with his worshippers. Then this verse came: {reward}those for whom good has gone ahead from Allah are kept far from it{/reward}.
now: You worry: what if I'm swept up with everyone else? {idea}Allah's justice separates.{/idea} {reward}Those who lived for Him are kept far{/reward}, even if others misused their names.
old: On the Day, I might be lumped in with everyone around me.
new: Allah separates. Those who lived for Him are kept far from the Fire.
try: Ask Allah today to make you one of those for whom good has gone ahead.

title: Not even its faintest sound, and everything they desire.
subtitle: Safe from fear, surrounded by what they love
then: The tafsir says the blessed {idea}will not feel its heat in their bodies{/idea}. They will be {reward}safe from what they fear, and have all that they love and desire{/reward}. Just as they did good in this world, Allah makes their final destiny good.
now: The neighbour's renovation noise, the traffic, the constant alerts. You crave just a little quiet. {reward}Imagine complete safety, with everything your heart wants.{/reward} {idea}That is what doing good here leads to.{/idea}
old: The best I can hope for is just to escape punishment.
new: Allah promises not just safety but everything the heart desires.
try: Spend two minutes picturing Paradise as the verse describes, then make dua for it.

title: The greatest terror will not grieve them; angels greet them.
subtitle: Calm on the most frightening day
then: After describing the deniers, Allah describes the blessed: {reward}the greatest terror will not grieve them{/reward}. The angels will meet them with the words, {idea}this is your Day which you were promised{/idea}.
now: You think of the Day of Judgement with dread, like the worst exam of your life. {reward}For those who lived for Allah, it is the day they were waiting for{/reward}, with angels at the door.
old: The Day of Judgement is only something to dread.
new: For the believers it is a promised day, met with angels' greeting.
try: Next time you think of the Day with fear, add hope: ask to be greeted by the angels.

title: The sky rolled up like a scroll, and creation begun again.
subtitle: The One who began creation will repeat it
then: On the Day of Resurrection the heaven will be rolled up like a scroll. Ibn 'Abbas said the word means {idea}the record, rolled up{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said people will be gathered {trap}barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised{/trap}, then recited: as We began the first creation, We will repeat it.
now: You fold a letter, roll up a poster, close a notebook full of a year's plans. {idea}That is how easily Allah will fold the sky.{/idea} {reward}He made you once from nothing; making you again is a promise He keeps.{/reward}
old: It is hard to imagine the whole world ending and starting again.
new: The One who began creation will repeat it. It is His promise.
try: Close your notebook or laptop tonight and remember: one Day the sky will fold like this.

title: It was written long ago: My righteous servants inherit the land.
subtitle: A promise recorded in the earlier Books
then: Ibn 'Abbas, Ash-Sha'bi and others said the Zabur was revealed to Dawud, and the Reminder is the Tawrah. {idea}Allah wrote in them that His righteous servants would inherit the land.{/idea} Ibn 'Abbas said {reward}this means the land of Paradise{/reward}.
now: You see people cheat their way to the big house and the corner office. {trap}It looks like they own everything.{/trap} {reward}The lasting inheritance was written long ago for the righteous.{/reward}
old: The people who grab the most end up with the most.
new: The lasting inheritance belongs to Allah's righteous servants. It is written.
try: Choose the honest option in one small money matter today, trusting that inheritance.

title: In this Quran is a clear message for people who worship.
subtitle: Enough guidance for anyone who wants it

row.title: more sources
sub: one more book, one more talk

then: The tafsir says the Quran is {reward}a plain message, beneficial and sufficient{/reward} for a people who worship Allah. These are people {idea}who would rather obey Allah than follow Shaytan or their own desires{/idea}.
now: You save posts, buy books, bookmark talks, and feel you never know enough to begin. {trap}Collecting feels like progress.{/trap} {reward}The guidance you need is already in your hands.{/reward}
old: I need to learn much more before I can really live my faith.
new: The Quran is enough for someone who wants to worship. I can start with what I know.
try: Act on one verse you already know today instead of looking for something new.

title: He was sent only as a mercy to all the worlds.
subtitle: The Prophet as the gift the Makkans called a problem
then: The surah introduction says the Makkans considered him a distress, but {reward}he had come as a blessing{/reward}. When asked to pray against the idolaters, he said: {idea}I was not sent as a curse; I was sent as a mercy{/idea}. Ibn 'Abbas said even those who rejected him were spared what struck earlier nations.
now: Someone annoys you at work and you want to snap. {idea}The one you follow was sent as mercy, even to those who opposed him.{/idea} {reward}You carry a little of that mercy into every room.{/reward}
old: Being religious means being strict and hard on people.
new: The Prophet ﷺ was sent as mercy. Following him means being merciful.
try: Treat one difficult person today with deliberate gentleness.

title: The whole message: your God is one. Will you submit?
subtitle: Revelation boiled down to one question
then: Near the end, the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}it is revealed to me that your God is only one God{/idea}. The tafsir calls this the main objective of revelation, that Allah be worshipped. Then the question: {reward}will you follow and submit to it?{/reward}
now: You believe Allah is one. You'd say it without blinking. {trap}The question is whether your week shows it.{/trap} {idea}Submission is belief that reaches your calendar, your wallet, your tongue.{/idea}
old: I already believe Allah is one; that is the main thing.
new: Believing He is one is the start. Submitting to Him is the answer the verse asks for.
try: Pick one area of life you keep separate from faith, and bring Allah into it today.

title: If they turn away: I have told you all equally.
subtitle: Delivering the message clearly, then stepping back
then: If they ignored his call, he was to say: {idea}I have informed you all alike{/idea}. The tafsir compares it to: for me my deeds and for you yours. And on the Hour: {trap}it will surely come, but I do not know whether it is near or far{/trap}.
now: You have told your brother your concern about his choices, clearly and kindly. He disagrees. {trap}You keep pushing and it gets worse.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes your part is done once the message is clear.{/idea}
old: If someone doesn't accept what I say, I have to keep pressing.
new: My job is to say it clearly and kindly. The rest is between them and Allah.
try: Let go of one argument you keep restarting. Make dua for that person instead.

title: He knows what you say out loud and what you hide.
subtitle: The open and the hidden, equally known
then: The tafsir says Allah {idea}knows the unseen in its entirety{/idea}: what His creatures do openly and what they do secretly. {trap}He will repay them for it, both minor and major.{/trap} The surah opened with the Prophet ﷺ saying his Lord knows every word.
now: The polite smile in the meeting, and the thought behind it. The kind post online, and the comment you typed and deleted. {idea}Allah knows both versions of you.{/idea} {reward}Making them match is a kind of peace.{/reward}
old: What people see is what matters.
new: Allah knows what I show and what I hide. I want the two to match.
try: Notice one gap today between what you say and what you think. Close it a little.

title: Perhaps the delay is a test, and enjoyment for a while.
subtitle: Why ease without consequences can be a trial
then: The Prophet ﷺ said he did not know; {trap}perhaps it is a trial for you, and an enjoyment for a while{/trap}. Ibn Jarir explained it as {idea}being delayed as a test, with enjoyment for an allotted time{/idea}.
now: You did something wrong and nothing happened. No one found out. Life carried on. {trap}It feels like you got away with it.{/trap} {idea}The quiet afterwards may be the test itself.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad happened, it was not a big deal.
new: A delay is not a pardon. It may be time given to turn back.
try: Take one wrong you got away with and quietly repair it or seek forgiveness.

title: My Lord, judge in truth. We seek the Merciful's help.
subtitle: The surah's last word: handing it all to Allah
then: The prophets used to say: {idea}our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth{/idea}. Zayd bin Aslam said when the Prophet ﷺ witnessed fighting, he would say: my Lord, judge in truth. The surah ends seeking {reward}the help of the Most Merciful{/reward} against all their fabrications.
now: Someone spreads lies about you, and you lie awake drafting replies. {idea}This verse is a better reply{/idea}: my Lord, judge in truth. {reward}Then lean on the Most Merciful and sleep.{/reward}
old: I have to set every record straight myself.
new: I can hand the judgment to Allah and seek the Merciful's help. That is enough.
try: Tonight, about one thing said against you, say: Rabbi uhkum bil-haqq, and leave it there.
